reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the desirability of Cr2O3 and Al2O3 and the protective role of Cr2O3, but it does not provide direct evidence that increasing Cr/Al in multiprincipal-element alloys leads to the predicted outcomes; the key mechanistic premise about composition adjustment is unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Cr2O3 and Al2O3 are desirable protective oxides for high-temperature alloys
Cr2O3 has a compact structure and superior oxidation resistance
Absence of a Cr2O3 layer can lead to outward diffusion of Mn and formation of less protective Mn3O4
